observations: Photo 0 shows a light teal air fryer with a black power cord and a European-style plug. The brand name 'KOMOO' is visible below the control dial. The unit is partially wrapped in plastic.
Photo 1 shows the same teal air fryer with the basket pulled out, revealing a black perforated basket. The control panel has a single dial and two buttons. The brand 'KOMOO' is visible again.
Photo 2 shows a different air fryer, black with a silver control panel and two dials. It also has a European-style plug and is wrapped in plastic. The brand is not visible on this unit.
All three photos have a watermark 'POSTED ON JIJI OLISAEMEKA MAKOJOO'.
The seller claims it is an 'Airfyer London', but the photos show 'KOMOO' branding, not 'Airfyer London'.

claims.evidence: Photos 0 and 1 show the brand 'KOMOO' on the front panel, not 'Airfyer London'. Photo 2 shows a different air fryer with no visible brand.
This is a subjective quality claim; no visible damage or wear is evident, but durability cannot be assessed from photos alone.
No photo shows the unit in operation or any testing. The seller's statement is unverified by visual evidence.

risks.risk: The European plug may not be compatible with Nigerian power outlets without an adapter.
risks.proof: A photo of the plug inserted into a Nigerian socket or a clear shot of the plug type with a label.

risks.risk: The air fryer may have hidden wear, scratches, or damage under the plastic wrap.
risks.proof: A close-up photo of the unit without plastic wrap, showing all surfaces.

proof_requests: A video of the air fryer operating, including turning on, heating, and cycling through settings.
A photo of the unit without plastic wrap, showing all sides and condition.
A clear photo of the plug inserted into a Nigerian socket or a label confirming compatibility.
response.reason: The seller's claim of 'Airfyer London' is contradicted by the visible 'KOMOO' branding. The unit's working condition and compatibility with Nigerian outlets are unverified. Without proof of operation and full condition, a worst-case price cannot be confidently assigned.
